newsitem.title: CHINA: China says speeding up border talks with Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: China says speeding up border talks with Vietnam.

text.p: China and Vietnam are speeding up efforts to resolve simmering territorial disputes along the land and sea borders dividing the communist neighbours, Beijing's official Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen agreed with his Vietnamese counterpart Nguyen Manh Cam that Beijing and Hanoi should tackle more easily resolved issues first and put aside the thornier disputes for later, Xinhua said.
Cam was in Beijing as part of a delegation accompanying Vietnam Communist Party General Secretary Muoi, who is making a five-day visit to China.

During their meeting at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse, both foreign ministers had agreed that talks between Muoi and Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Monday had been a strong boost to strengthening Sino-Vietnamese cooperation, Xinhua said.

"The foreign ministries... are responsible for resolutely implementing a new consensus reached by top leaders of the two nations on speeding up the progress of border talks," it quoted Qian and Cam as saying.
The effort to accelerate negotiations included disputes over the Sino-Vietnamese land border as well as on territory in the oil and gas rich Tonkin Gulf, it said.
Hanoi and Beijing also are among several regional claimants to the potentially resource-rich Spratly islands in the South China Sea.
Vietnam said in April it had agreed with China to accelerate the pace of talks on some of their borders, which have remained a source of dispute between them since they fought a border war in 1979.
Relations between Hanoi and Beijing have eased in recent years, but territorial issues have continued to strain the socialist rapprochement.
Tensions boiled over in March, when a Chinese oil rig began exploratory drilling in a contested area of the South China Sea about 64.5 nautical miles off the coast of central Vietnam.
The rig was withdrawn after less than a month, but the two sides failed to resolve their differences on the issue at an emergency meeting in Beijing in April.
Settlement of border problems would open broad prospects for the development of Sino-Vietnamese relations, Xinhua quoted China's Qian as saying.
